To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MM-based algorithms developed by CRPsM to count the refugee camps population, based on VHSR satellite images, have been successfully applied to several camps located in Africa.
we have developed a method that allows the detection of refugee camps, in a completely automatic way, using only the information provided by VHSR satellite images.

we developed a new algorithm for the detection of tents in refugee camps, based on mathematical morphology, and we compared our algorithm to the one developed in the eCognition platform, and to other already available algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology that allows to automatically detect and count the number of tents in refugee camps.
the development of automatic techniques for the estimation of refugee camps populations, by means of VHSR satellite images.
the development and validation of automatic techniques for the extraction of tents in refugee camps from VHSR satellite data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed algorithms are very promising for a fast and reliable tents detection in refugee camps.

the MM based techniques are able to detect tents with a very good accuracy and that they are able to perform well also on a broad set of background conditions, including those ones where the tents are not clearly visible, due to the presence of shadows, etc.

the developed techniques are able to provide a satisfactory estimation of the number of tents (refugees) in a refugee camp, with a good accuracy, in terms of both the number of detected objects and their location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MM-based algorithms developed by CRP are more accurate than the others in detecting tents in refugee camps, and that the developed procedures can be applied to a broader set (in terms of background conditions) of VHSR satellite images than the other ones.
we have developed new algorithms to improve performances and to extend their application to broader set of background condition.
the mathematical morphology is a powerful tool to detect tents in refugee camps, but the results are not always as accurate as the ones obtained using other methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even though there are many methods to detect refugee camps, the problem of detecting tents is still an open issue.
the MM based techniques are more effective than other available algorithms, in terms of detection rate and precision.

MM is an effective and efficient tool to solve the problem of tents counting, even when the background conditions (e.g., the presence of vegetation) are not optimal for the application of the other techniques.
